title: Return an Error
story: Go has no exceptions. A function returns an error and the caller checks it.
goal: Write Divide(a, b float64) (float64, error). Dividing by zero returns an error with the message division by zero.
hints: Check b == 0 first and return early with errors.New(...).
On success return the result and nil.
socratic: What does nil mean for an error?
What should the number be when there is an error?
Why does Go make you check err yourself?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Return an Error”?
